motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Agreement with Identity Signs for Six Wayfinding Signs. Finance Management Analyst Terrence Dela Pena presented the item. Wayfinding signs currently exist throughout the City; these are deteriorating due to exposure to weather conditions and the usual wear and tear for their allowable functionality and appearance. Some signs have become problematic for visibility issues, while others are needed to direct the public to new parks such as Smith Ranch Park and other existing city parks. The new wayfinding signs will adopt the new branding logo and colors, which will support the overall look and feel the City Council, residents, and Staff want for the community. The panels are adjustable and can be changed depending on Eagle Mountain City Council Meeting – July 2, 2024 Page 6 of 11 which city facilities or amenities need to be highlighted. The timeline will depend primarily on the availability of the wood post, and staff hopes the signs can be installed before the end of fall this year.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to deny the approval of a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, for an Agreement with Identity Signs for Six Wayfinding Signs with instructions to staff to find a more durable material for the signs and a lower installation cost option. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Professional Services Agreement with REDKOR Brand Campaigns to Create a Marketing Plan. This item was discussed after item 14.A. Communications Manager Tyler Maffitt presented the item. Communications Manager Tyler Maffitt presented the item. Eagle Mountain City is pursuing this contract to develop a more comprehensive and cohesive messaging strategy. The goal is to ensure that all communications, whether related to tourism, economic development, or other City initiatives, are consistent, agreed upon, and effective in reaching their intended audiences. This strategic approach is intended to achieve outcomes and fully unify the City's voice while enhancing its overall communication efforts now and into the future.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve of a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Professional Services Agreement with REDKOR Brand Campaigns to Create a Marketing Plan, with a month-to-month plan of $3,500 per month that can be discontinued at any time, with a benchmark plan with Eagle Mountain City Council Meeting – July 2, 2024 Page 7 of 11 economic portion of the scope of work frontloaded, and not to exceed 14 months. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Enacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.32, Historic Zones. Senior Planner Robert Hobbs presented the item. The proposed ordinance enacts Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.32, Historic Zones to assist the City in sharing and enforcing its development rules in a consistent and legally supportable manner, while awaiting rezoning of some properties in the community to bring them into compliance with 2024 codes. This item was tabled at the June 18, 2024 City Council meeting.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Enacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.32, Historic Zones, to be brought back to the August 6, 2024 City Council meeting. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
